summary.oneLiner: The Grob Tea Company Ltd is an Assam-based tea plantation and manufacturing company producing CTC, orthodox, and green teas for domestic and export markets.
summary.business: The Grob Tea Company Ltd owns and operates tea estates in Assam, cultivating and manufacturing black CTC and orthodox teas, as well as green tea. The company sells its tea primarily through auction centers and private sales to domestic buyers, with a portion directed to export markets. Its operations are vertically integrated from plantation to processing, relying on a large workforce across its estates.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: The Grob Tea Company Ltd is an Assam-based tea plantation and manufacturing company producing CTC, orthodox, and green teas for domestic and export markets.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Grob Tea Company Ltd owns and operates tea estates in Assam, cultivating and manufacturing black CTC and orthodox teas, as well as green tea. The company sells its tea primarily through auction centers and private sales to domestic buyers, with a portion directed to export markets. Its operations are vertically integrated from plantation to processing, relying on a large workforce across its estates.

end_markets.body:
- Domestic Indian market (auction centers and private sales)
- Export markets

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Current year started with early drought-like weather which improved as the season progressed; Jorhat & Golaghat districts experienced favourable growing conditions, helping Doyang & Dessoi estates increase production by 64% and 66% respectively.
- Market has so far been quite steady and buoyant with an average increase in price realization of Rs.45 per kg over the previous year.
- Early indication shows export is likely to further go up provided the geo-political situation remains favourable, which is likely to make the domestic market strong and stable.
- Increase of export with lesser retention should make the market stable and strong, but import of cheap varieties of tea getting mixed up with domestic production is a matter of serious concern.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Mitigate climate-change impact on tea production through a comprehensive project (PWCC) to improve micro-climate around gardens and enhance irrigation capacity and efficiency.
- Maintain cordial industrial relations and invest in employee development and wellbeing as a labour-intensive operation.
- The Board has recommended a dividend of Rs. 2/- per equity share of Rs. 10/- each for FY26, subject to shareholder approval. The company's governance philosophy emphasizes transparency, accountability, and long-term stakeholder value creation.
- Comprehensive project on climate change (PWCC) to mitigate ill-effects and improve micro-climate around gardens; improving capacity and efficiency of existing irrigation sets to minimize early drought impact.
- Endeavour to provide safe, healthy and sustainable work environment in all estates for employees and their families; employee empowerment across the organization; cordial industrial relations with zero employee disputes during the year.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company has undertaken a comprehensive project called 'Project Work on Climate Change' (PWCC) to mitigate the ill-effects of erratic weather and improve the micro-climate around its tea gardens. As part of this initiative, the capacity and efficiency of existing irrigation sets are being improved to a large extent to minimize the impact of early drought. The MD&A notes that climate change has altered monsoon patterns, leading to longer dry spells and shorter periods of heavy rain, which this project aims to address. Additionally, the Debt Service Coverage Ratio variance explanation indicates an increase in term loans for capital expenditure, though specific capex projects beyond PWCC and irrigation improvements are not detailed.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Vertically integrated operations from tea plantation to processing, ensuring control over quality and supply chain.
- Established presence in Assam's key tea-growing regions (Jorhat and Golaghat) with favorable micro-climates supporting production recovery.
- Long-standing industry experience and stable workforce of over 3,781 employees, with cordial industrial relations.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Climate change and erratic weather patterns — Tea crop is totally rain-dependent; global warming causes high ambient temperatures and erratic rainfall (long dry spells, short heavy rains), jeopardizing production across all tea-growing regions, especially North East India.
- Labour shortage and rising costs — Tea is a labour-intensive industry; shortage of labour during peak season, substantial increases in labour costs, high social costs, and other input costs remain a major structural concern.
- Increasing dominance of small tea growers (STGs) and declining organized sector share — Organized sector production share dropped to 43% (down 3% YoY) while STG share rose to 57%, a steadily continuing structural shift that pressures organized players.
- Import of cheap tea varieties mixing with domestic production — Cheap imported teas getting blended with domestic production is a serious concern that can undermine domestic price stability and quality perception.
- Price realization volatility — Despite higher exports, much higher domestic retention led to a 9% drop in average Assam CTC price realization; profitability is highly sensitive to sale price fluctuations.
- Geopolitical risk to export momentum — Record exports of 280 M kgs (up 9% YoY) are expected to rise further only if the geopolitical situation remains favourable, making export-led market stability conditional.
